title: Le Corbusier's birth chart
metaDescription: Le Corbusier's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.9° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.0° separates the Sun and Uranus from an exact conjunction; at that range identity and disruption read as one mechanism. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 12.9° Libra, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Venus in Virgo (21.1°), Mars in Leo (25.2°): attraction that grows by reliability, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: the Sun to Uranus, a conjunction with 0.0° of slack. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, Saturn sextile Pluto at 0.1°, and Jupiter square Saturn at 4.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Venus makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, three placements stand out. The Sun in Libra at 12.9° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Virgo at 21.1° is in fall; Saturn in Leo at 4.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives air 3, earth 2, fire 2, water 1, and fixed 4, cardinal 2, mutable 2 across the modes. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. Mercury crossed from Libra into Scorpio during that day, so its sign is left open. Venus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.1° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
